objective: Freeze a benchmark-independent V3 smoke-probe contract before executing it on development repositories.

required_provenance: explicit top-level import names where present
declared console entry points where present
prohibited_inference: guessing import names from distribution names
using source-directory import success as installed-package evidence

probe_contract.package_import: Use fixed Python code with `python -I`; pass the validated module as an argv value.
probe_contract.entry_point_import: Import the declared entry-point module and resolve every declared attribute without invoking it.
probe_contract.cli_help: Invoke each validated console executable with `--help` as a direct argv vector.

decision_contract.pass: At least one semantic import probe is planned, every planned probe has an observed zero exit code, no metadata item is rejected, and every declared console entry point has both import and CLI coverage.
decision_contract.fail: Any observed planned probe exits nonzero or times out.
decision_contract.unknown: Required metadata or outcomes are missing, no semantic import probe can be planned, or metadata is rejected as unsafe/ambiguous.

synthetic_counterexamples: No metadata produces unknown rather than pass.
A distribution name is never converted into an import name.
Invalid module, attribute, or executable names are rejected.
A timeout or nonzero exit produces fail.
Source working-directory masking is prevented by isolated mode and an empty working directory.
Every declared console entry point requires both target import and CLI probes.
